long.description:
In 1200 AD, Angkor was the biggest city on Earth — a million people in a city built of water and stone. Within a century, the jungle had swallowed it whole. I traced the rise and fall of the Khmer Empire, from the god-king crowned in 802 to the laser scans that finally revealed the true city.

The truth is stranger than any single villain: the most advanced water machine of the ancient world, decades of failed monsoons, a sack by a rival kingdom — and a jungle that never stopped growing. But here's the twist most people miss: Angkor was never truly lost. Buddhist monks kept its temples alive for six hundred years while the world forgot.

This is the story of the megacity the jungle swallowed — and the warning it carries for our own cities.
